articles/hacoo-order-tracking.title: Hacoo Order Tracking: Statuses, Delays & Next Steps
articles/hacoo-order-tracking.intro: Find the right tracking number, understand fulfilment and delivery updates, and prepare useful evidence when a Hacoo parcel stops moving.
sections: Start with the order record, not a product link

To track a Hacoo order, start with the order details in the account used for the purchase. Look for the shipment information, carrier name and tracking number associated with that order. A product ID identifies a listing; it cannot locate a parcel. An order number identifies the purchase; it may also differ from the number accepted by the delivery carrier. Copy each value into a separate field so that a support request does not mix three unrelated identifiers. This independent guide cannot see private orders or provide a live tracking service.

Before interpreting a delay, record the purchase date, dispatch date if shown, destination country and delivery window displayed for your order. Save a screenshot of the latest status with its timestamp. If several items were ordered, check whether they share a shipment. A missing item may belong to another parcel, so avoid assuming the first delivered package completes the whole order. Use the order's own shipment details to establish which items and tracking numbers belong together.
Read the latest scan as an event, not a promise

Tracking usually describes events that have already been recorded. A label-created message can mean that shipment information exists without confirming a physical carrier collection. An acceptance scan is stronger evidence of a handover. An in-transit message describes movement within a network, but it does not necessarily mean the parcel is already in your country. Status wording differs between carriers, languages and interfaces. Read the complete event history instead of treating a translated headline as a universal definition.

Terms such as fulfilment hub, sorting centre or processing facility normally describe a handling stage. The words alone do not establish the country, an exact delivery date or a problem. Check the location, timestamp and the following event. If location information is missing, keep that uncertainty in your notes. Repeated scans at one facility may be routine processing or an exception; distinguish them using any additional message. Do not invent a deadline from a hub name or count every repeated event as another shipping day.
Separate preparation, transport and local delivery

A useful delivery timeline has separate stages: preparing the order, handing it to a carrier, moving it between facilities and completing local delivery. A preparation delay needs an order-status question, while an attempted local delivery needs an address or collection check. Treating both as 'tracking not updating' makes support harder. Write the current stage at the top of your notes, together with the evidence that places the parcel there. If no carrier acceptance appears, say that rather than claiming the package is lost in transit.

Hacoo's public shipping pages give general estimates, and the published ranges are not identical across pages and destinations. Use the delivery window attached to your actual order as the practical reference; a general guide cannot guarantee its arrival date. Also keep calendar days and working days separate. Weekends, holidays, an international handover or missing scans can make the visible timeline look different from the physical journey. Do not add overlapping published stage estimates to manufacture a precise total.
When Hacoo tracking is not updating

First compare the timestamp of the last genuine event with the delivery window, rather than comparing today's date with the purchase date alone. Refresh the order view and check the carrier information shown there. Copy the number carefully, preserving letters and leading zeroes. If the order provides a second tracking number for local delivery, record the relationship between the original number and the local one. A number that fails in the wrong carrier's system does not prove that the parcel does not exist.

Next identify the useful question. If dispatch is not confirmed, ask whether preparation is complete. If a carrier accepted the parcel but nothing changed, ask which carrier currently holds it and whether an investigation is available. If the estimated window has passed, include that window and the last scan in the message. There is no reliable universal rule that every silent period means loss after a fixed number of days. Avoid repeated identical requests; keep one case history with dates and the support response.
Handle delivery exceptions with the right evidence

An attempted-delivery event should prompt a check of the delivery instructions, address and any collection notice. Compare the address on the order with the real destination, including apartment details and postcode. Use the contact route shown in the order to ask about another attempt or collection arrangements. Do not assume changing your profile address also changes an existing shipment. When an address is wrong, explain it promptly and ask what can still be corrected at the current stage.

If tracking says delivered but you cannot find the parcel, check the mailbox, designated safe place and whether a household member or neighbour accepted it. Ask for the delivery evidence associated with the tracking number. Keep the order and carrier replies together. A returned-to-sender status requires a different request: establish the stated reason and ask support whether redelivery or a refund is available for that order. Neither outcome should be promised by an independent article. Preserve the original status even if it later changes.
Build a short support request that can be acted on

Useful support messages describe one order, one problem and one requested next step. Include the order number, relevant shipment number, last event and date, destination country, displayed delivery window and a short description of what you have already checked. Attach a clear screenshot instead of a long sequence of cropped fragments. If the carrier has given a case number, include it. Share full address and payment information only through the authenticated support channel when required, not in public comments or social posts.

For example, explain that the carrier recorded acceptance on a stated date, no later event is visible, and the order's estimated window has ended. Ask who currently holds the parcel and what investigation step is available. This is a template for organising facts, not a claim about your parcel. If the reply requests additional evidence, add it to the existing case where possible. Record the date and the promised follow-up action so that the next message can refer to a specific unresolved point.
Keep parcel problems separate from product problems

Tracking answers where a shipment is in the delivery process. It does not tell you whether the correct size, colour or quantity is inside. After delivery, compare the received item with the exact option saved at purchase. Keep the packaging and identify which item belongs to which order. Photograph a mismatch before using, washing or altering the item. A delivered tracking event and an incorrect item can both be true, and the evidence for each issue is different.

For a partial delivery, compare the order's item list with every shipment before reporting a missing unit. For visible transport damage, record the condition of the outside packaging as well as the item, when it is safe to do so. For a product defect, take an overall image and a close view that shows its location. Keep the support request focused on what you can demonstrate. The QC photo guide and returns guide explain how to organise this evidence without turning a tracking dispute into an unsupported quality claim.
Use a repeatable tracking record

A compact record is more useful than checking the same page every few minutes. Keep the order number, shipment numbers, carrier, last scan, delivery window and support case in one place. Add a new line only when an event or response changes. This makes it possible to distinguish a genuine update from the same message displayed again. It also helps another household member understand what has already been checked without opening multiple accounts or starting a duplicate support conversation.

Before taking the next step, confirm three things: which shipment is affected, what the most recent evidence actually says, and which action is now possible. Wait within the displayed estimate when no exception is reported, investigate a missed estimate with the relevant support channel, and respond promptly to an address or collection request. These are decision checks, not delivery guarantees. If you are still researching an item and have no order, use the spreadsheet and product-link guides first; a listing code is not a tracking code.
takeaways: Use shipment tracking numbers, not product IDs.
Compare the last scan with the order's delivery window.
Ask about the current stage with a concise evidence record.
Keep delivery, item quality and refund issues distinct.

articles/hacoo-search-no-results.title: Hacoo Search Not Working: No Results & Missing Products
articles/hacoo-search-no-results.intro: Troubleshoot empty Hacoo searches, missing products and old links with a clear sequence for your query, app, region and product identity.
sections: Identify which search is failing

When Hacoo search shows no results, first identify the surface you are using: the official app, a web page, an independent spreadsheet or a linked product catalog. They are separate systems and may not accept the same identifiers. A code copied from one catalog is not automatically searchable in another. This site's search opens an external product catalog; it is not an official Hacoo app search and cannot inspect your account. Record where you searched before trying to explain the result.

Describe the failure precisely. An empty results list, an error message, a link opening the homepage and a product with no selectable size are different problems. Save the query as plain text and note the date, device, app version if available and actual delivery country. Take a screenshot showing the result and search field, avoiding private account details. This small record makes each retry comparable. Without it, a changed query or a different catalog can look like an app repair when it is simply another search.
Test a simple, descriptive query

Start with a short product description instead of a full social-media caption. A noun plus one distinctive feature is often easier to interpret: zip hoodie, canvas shoulder bag or low-top shoe. Remove emojis, hashtags, promotional language and unrelated words. Keep the original query in your notes so you can compare it with the simplified version. Try one spelling correction at a time. The goal is to learn whether the search works generally before investigating why one particular item is missing.

If a simple query returns relevant items, add a second meaningful feature such as colour or construction. If results disappear, the added word may be too restrictive or absent from listing titles. That does not prove the item is unavailable. Conversely, broad results do not prove you have found the original product. Treat each result as a candidate until its identifier, image and options match. Avoid treating popular coupon phrases as product names: a discount code, product ID and tracking number have different purposes.
Check product codes without confusing their source

A product identifier is most useful when the destination explicitly labels it as an item or product ID. Copy it exactly, retaining leading zeroes and avoiding spaces inserted by messaging apps. A number in a URL may instead be a website's internal page number. An image filename, style label or order number is not a substitute. Keep the source catalog next to the identifier so that a later search uses the appropriate system rather than expecting every number to work everywhere.

Try the current direct product route when you have one. If it loads, compare the visible identifier with your saved record. If it does not load, search a neutral description and compare the candidates manually. Never declare the first similar image a replacement. For example, two bags may share a silhouette but have different dimensions, closures or included straps. An exact recovery needs enough matching fields to justify the claim; otherwise label the result as an alternative and keep the original unresolved.
Confirm your real region and delivery destination

Regional settings and delivery eligibility can affect what you see, but a missing result alone cannot establish the reason. Check that the account and delivery destination reflect your real location. Review any explicit availability message on the product page. A product visible in a shared screenshot may no longer be offered for the same destination or option. Record what the interface actually says instead of attributing every empty search to a country restriction.

Do not use a false address, another person's account or location-masking tricks to force a catalog view. Seeing an item under an artificial setting does not establish that it can be delivered to you, and it can introduce new checkout problems. If the real destination is not supported, stop that purchase path and ask the platform about availability. This guide offers a way to diagnose the discrepancy; it does not promise that changing settings will unlock a product or restore an old catalog.
Rule out a local app or browser issue

Check whether the rest of the app loads normally and whether a second ordinary query works. If the interface itself is unresponsive, confirm your connection, close and reopen the app, and look for an update through the official app store. In a browser, try reopening the current destination without a stale saved tab. Change one variable at a time and record the outcome. This keeps a temporary connection failure separate from an item that genuinely does not appear in search.

Avoid installing unofficial application packages or entering credentials into a page that claims to repair search. Before signing out or clearing app data, make sure you can recover the account through its normal sign-in method. Do not delete useful order screenshots while troubleshooting. If several unrelated queries fail on the same up-to-date app, document the pattern and contact support. Individual reports of empty results are useful clues, but they do not establish a platform-wide outage or a confirmed cause for your account.
Recover a product from an old link or screenshot

Old links and screenshots preserve different kinds of evidence. A link may preserve a route or identifier, while a screenshot may show the style, selected colour, dimensions or option label. Write down those clues before searching. Follow the original route and note its final destination. A redirect to the homepage should be recorded as a failed product route, not a successful match. If the page opens another item, stop using that URL as proof of the original product.

Build a small candidate list and compare one item at a time. Check the first image, title, identifier, selected option, dimensions and what is included. Price can flag a mismatch but cannot prove identity by itself. Save the matching fields and the fields still unknown. If no candidate meets the important clues, preserve the old record as unresolved instead of publishing a confident replacement. The dedicated old-link recovery guide provides a deeper workflow, while the spreadsheet offers a structured place to begin comparing current entries.
Recognise when searching cannot solve availability

A search can locate information; it cannot restore a removed listing or a sold-out option. If the product opens but the required size cannot be selected, the problem is option availability rather than an empty-search error. If the platform explicitly reports removal or destination restrictions, respect that information. Do not repeatedly switch keywords in the hope that an unavailable option becomes orderable. Record the status and decide whether to wait for official information or compare a clearly labelled alternative.

Before choosing an alternative, restate the features you need. For clothing, that may include actual measurements, fabric description and set contents; for a bag, dimensions and closure; for shoes, the size system and insole information. Compare those fields rather than choosing the closest marketing image. Keep alternatives under their own identifiers. This prevents a discovery guide from silently changing what an old recommendation means and helps readers make a new decision with current evidence.
Send a reproducible report and retain the result

A useful search report includes the exact query, where it was entered, the app version or browser, real destination, time of the test and the visible result. Explain whether a simple unrelated query worked and whether the direct product route still opens. Attach one screenshot showing the issue and another only if it provides a different necessary fact. Do not send passwords, payment details or a full private order history to explain a search problem.

After support responds or the search starts working, repeat the same original test before calling the issue resolved. Then verify the product identity and option again; a working results page is only the beginning of product research. Save the current route with its actual check date. Use the product-ID guide for identifier questions, the broken-link guide for redirects, and the QC and size guides before deciding on a purchase. This sequence turns repeated guessing into a record that another person can understand and reproduce.
takeaways: Identify the app or catalog being searched.
Test a short description, then verify the product ID and option.
Use your real destination and official app updates.
Treat unavailable products and broken search as different problems.

articles/hacoo-returns-refunds.title: Hacoo Returns & Refunds: Evidence, Requests & Follow-Up
articles/hacoo-returns-refunds.intro: Prepare a clear Hacoo return or refund request, keep the right photos, follow order-specific instructions and distinguish approval from money received.
sections: Begin with the policy attached to your order

For a Hacoo return or refund, first open the affected order and review the current after-sales instructions. Hacoo's public return policy describes a general fifteen-day period after receipt for most eligible products, with category exceptions. That is a published starting point, not a guarantee that every item or situation qualifies. Save the policy or instructions shown for your actual purchase and the date the item arrived. This independent guide does not decide eligibility, issue labels or process money.

Act promptly when you notice a problem. Separate the date of delivery from the date you first wore or inspected the item; a personal inspection delay does not necessarily change the stated request window. If delivery is disputed or the parcel has not arrived, explain that situation instead of selecting an inaccurate product-return reason. Where different public pages use different wording, ask support to confirm the process for your order in writing. Keep that response with the purchase record before sending anything back.
Describe the problem in observable terms

Choose a reason that matches what happened: the wrong item, an incomplete set, visible damage, an inaccurate measurement, a delivery problem or a change of mind. These cases require different evidence and may be treated differently. Describe the discrepancy in one sentence before attaching photographs. For example, identify the ordered colour and the received colour, or the measurement advertised and the measurement taken using the same method. Avoid vague statements such as 'bad quality' when a specific defect can be shown.

Check the selected option saved at purchase. A listing may include several versions or show a set in the lead image while the chosen option contains only one piece. Compare the order confirmation, option label and description rather than relying on memory. If the selected option was different from what you intended, explain that honestly. A precise account helps support understand whether the issue concerns fulfilment, product condition, listing information or a preference change, without turning uncertainty into an unsupported accusation.
Photograph identity, context and detail

Build a small evidence set with three levels: an overall photograph identifying the item, a medium view locating the issue, and a clear close-up showing the defect or discrepancy. Include the relevant label or product code where it helps connect the photograph to the order. For a size issue, show the measuring tape's starting point and the full measurement on a flat item. Use the same measuring method as the listing where possible. Perspective and stretched fabric can otherwise make a comparison unreliable.

Keep the original photographs, even if you create an annotated copy to highlight the problem. Avoid filters that change colour or conceal detail. If the parcel arrived damaged, record its outer condition and shipping label when safe, then connect the affected item to that parcel. Retain packaging, tags and accessories while the request is open. Do not expose your full address publicly when sharing images. Send necessary identifying details through the authenticated support channel, and use redacted copies for any public discussion.
Submit one complete request and save its reference

Use the after-sales route shown inside the order. Provide the order number, affected item and option, delivery date, concise reason and supporting photographs. If several items have different problems, identify each one clearly instead of making the whole order appear defective. State the outcome you are requesting, but allow support to confirm which remedies are available. Save the submitted text, case reference and timestamp so that a later follow-up refers to the same request.

Do not create several conflicting versions of the story across separate conversations. Add new evidence to the existing case when possible. If the form limits attachments, prioritise the images that establish identity and the issue, then mention that further originals are available. A confirmation that the request was received is not the same as approval. Read the response carefully for an evidence request, a proposed resolution or a return instruction. Each of those is a different next step and should be recorded separately.
Wait for confirmed return instructions before posting

Do not send an item to an address found in a blog, a parcel's origin label or an old support screenshot. Ask for the authorised destination and method for your order. The public policy allows different handling depending on the case, including situations where an item is returned and others where it is retained. Another shopper's outcome therefore cannot establish your own instructions. Keep the written authorisation, address, label if supplied and any deadline together.

Before packing, check the requested contents, original accessories and condition requirements. Photograph the item and package so you have a record of what was sent. Clarify who pays postage, whether a label is supplied and which tracking evidence must be kept. Do not assume the word 'free' removes every condition or covers a method you choose independently. Use the approved process, retain the shipping receipt and tracking number, and record the handover date. If the instructions are incomplete, ask a focused question before dispatch.
Distinguish review, approval and payment settlement

A refund request can pass through several separate stages: submission, review, a decision, any required return check, refund initiation and payment settlement. Track the stage that support has actually confirmed. A message saying the case is under review does not mean money has been sent. A message confirming initiation does not necessarily mean the credit is already visible at the bank. Keeping these stages separate prevents repeated requests based on the wrong starting date.

The public policy publishes processing estimates, but holidays, payment method and case requirements can affect the actual timeline. Ask which date starts the estimate quoted in your case and whether it refers to working days. Keep the approved amount, currency and payment reference. Compare the refund with the original transaction rather than assuming a different displayed currency means an error. If the credit is missing after the stated period, contact support with the initiation date and reference, then ask the payment provider to trace it if advised.
Follow up on the specific unresolved step

A useful follow-up identifies what has already happened and what remains unanswered. If evidence was submitted, ask whether anything else is needed for review. If the return was delivered, include its tracking confirmation and ask whether receipt has been registered. If the refund was initiated, ask for the transaction reference and applicable processing window. Avoid restarting the whole story when one stage can be checked directly. Keep replies in date order so the history is clear.

For a rejected request, read the stated reason and compare it with the order-specific policy and evidence. Correct a missing photo or mistaken item reference with factual clarification. Do not alter photographs or claim an item was unused when it was not. If the reply does not address the documented issue, ask for a review and point to the exact discrepancy. This guide describes an evidence workflow, not a legal determination or a promise that escalation will change the outcome. Retain the final written decision.
Reduce uncertainty before the next purchase

The strongest return record begins before payment. Save the current product ID, selected option, price, size chart, description and visible return conditions. For clothing, compare actual measurements with an item you own; for a set, record every included piece. For delivery-sensitive purchases, keep the estimate and real destination. These records make a later discrepancy easier to explain and may prevent an unsuitable purchase in the first place. A checked product link cannot replace those decisions.

When a case closes, confirm the practical outcome: the item was retained or returned according to instructions, the agreed amount reached the payment account, and no requested action remains open. Keep the essential evidence until that outcome is clear. For missing parcels, begin with the tracking guide; for visible product problems, use the QC photo checklist. Each guide supports a different stage. Following the order-specific process with a concise factual record is more useful than copying another buyer's refund story or assuming a universal result.
takeaways: Check the current order-specific policy and act promptly.
Show item identity, the problem and relevant measurements.
Return only through the authorised instructions.
Separate request receipt, approval and payment settlement.
